Source: A 30-year-old man presents to the emergency room with a laceration over the 4th metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint of his right hand.
His temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), pulse is 80/min, blood pressure is 125/75 mmHg, and respirations are 16/min.
He reports that he is a mailman, and his closed fist was bitten by a dog while he was delivering mail yesterday.
He reports pain but denies fevers, chills, drainage, or any other symptoms.
His last tetanus vaccine was 3 years ago.
The dog is up to date on vaccinations.
